records.title: Protocol for a randomised controlled trial of a web-based healthy relationship tool and safety decision aid for women experiencing domestic violence (I-DECIDE).
records.population_setting: Women 16-50y with recent partner abuse or fear, self-referred entirely online, Australia
records.key_finding: Describes a fully online, self-directed safety decision aid (I-DECIDE) built on the Psychosocial Readiness Model, delivering reflection exercises on relationship danger level and an individualised tailored action plan, with self-efficacy and depressive-symptom outcomes at 6 and 12 months.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports Layer 0 self-check design (self-directed reflection + individualised readout the person controls) and the private-channel/R2 concept; also the direct methodological ancestor of the T-PHE self-check model.

records.title: An online healthy relationship tool and safety decision aid for women experiencing intimate partner violence (I-DECIDE): a randomised controlled trial.
records.design: Pragmatic 2-arm RCT (masked, ITT), n=422 randomised (227 intervention/195 control)
records.population_setting: Women 16-50y screening positive for IPV or partner fear in Australia, entirely web-based recruitment/delivery
records.key_finding: 79-80% 12-month retention; self-efficacy was NOT improved and was in fact slightly LOWER in the intervention group than control at 6 months (mean difference 1.3, 95%CI 0.3-2.3) and 12 months (1.6, 95%CI 0.5-2.7); no between-group difference in depressive symptoms at 6 or 12 months.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates the assumption that an online self-assessment/decision aid improves self-efficacy or mental-health outcomes on validated quantitative measures - a null/adverse-direction primary-outcome result from the flagship trial in this literature; supports feasibility of anonymous web-only recruitment and high retention as a delivery model for Layer 0/R2.

records.title: I-DECIDE: An Online Intervention Drawing on the Psychosocial Readiness Model for Women Experiencing Domestic Violence.
records.population_setting: Conceptual - women experiencing domestic violence, informs the I-DECIDE Australian trial
records.key_finding: Argues that internet delivery can overcome disclosure barriers present in face-to-face health-care settings by letting a woman assess readiness and situate a plan within the Psychosocial Readiness Model before any external contact.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports the theoretical rationale for Layer 0 (self-check precedes and may substitute for disclosure to any programme actor) and for the person, not the programme, holding the readout.

records.title: Methodological and Ethical Challenges in a Web-Based Randomized Controlled Trial of a Domestic Violence Intervention.
records.design: Methodological/ethical case-study paper (reporting on the I-DECIDE RCT)
records.population_setting: Women in the I-DECIDE web-based DV trial, Australia
records.key_finding: Reports concrete recruitment, retention and safety/ethics challenges (e.g. verifying identity/safety online, risk of partner discovery, attrition) encountered running a domestic-violence RCT entirely on the web, and concludes such trials can be conducted safely with careful design.
records.relevance_to_tphe: directly informs the harms/failure-criterion element - documents real operational risks of an anonymous online self-assessment for IPV-adjacent content (partner discovery, verification, safe exit) that T-PHE's Layer 0 must design against.

records.title: A safety app to respond to dating violence for college women and their friends: the MyPlan study randomized controlled trial protocol.
records.population_setting: 300 abused college women + 300 concerned friends, Maryland and Oregon, USA
records.key_finding: Describes myPlan, a self-administered web/smartphone safety decision aid where users enter relationship-health and safety information and receive a personalised, priority-weighted safety plan they control, versus a static safety-planning control site.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports the scored, self-held-readout design pattern (user enters data, sees own tailored output) that Layer 0 adapts to premarital fear/control/reproductive/mental-health domains.

records.title: Longitudinal Impact of the myPlan App on Health and Safety Among College Women Experiencing Partner Violence.
records.population_setting: 346 college women (175 intervention/171 control), 41 colleges, Oregon and Maryland, USA
records.key_finding: Both arms improved on abuse, TBI-related IPV, digital abuse, reproductive coercion and depression over 12 months; reduction in reproductive coercion and improvement in suicide-risk were significantly greater in the myPlan self-decision-aid group than controls.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports that a self-directed decision aid can add incremental benefit specifically on reproductive-coercion and suicide-risk outcomes beyond generic safety information, relevant to T-PHE's reproductive/mental-health self-check domains.

records.title: Concerned friends of intimate partner violence survivors: results from the myPlan randomized controlled trial on college campuses.
records.population_setting: 293 college students (any gender) who were friends of an IPV survivor, 41 Oregon/Maryland colleges
records.key_finding: 89.2% of concerned friends worried their friend would be seriously hurt (22.7% extreme concern); myPlan-assigned friends showed significantly greater improvement in decisional conflict/understanding compared with usual web resources.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates a person-only framing - shows a decision-aid model also functions for third parties (peers/family) who might carry a Layer 0 readout forward, relevant to how a T-PHE self-check result could be shared voluntarily with a trusted other.

records.title: Effectiveness of the myPlan Teen App, a Digital Healthy Relationship and Safety Planning Intervention With Adolescents Aged 15-17 Years.
records.population_setting: 617 adolescents aged 15-17y, myPlan Teen vs usual care, USA
records.key_finding: myPlan Teen significantly increased use/helpfulness of safety behaviours and significantly reduced perpetration of physical/sexual violence and suicide behaviours versus control; victimisation and depression declined in both groups with no significant between-group difference.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports feasibility and selected efficacy of a self-directed digital safety/relationship tool in an adolescent (pre-adult, premarital-adjacent) population, though on a mixed outcome pattern - some outcomes null, informing T-PHE's own honest failure criterion.

records.title: Adapting the myPlan safety app to respond to intimate partner violence for women in low and middle income country settings: app tailoring and randomized controlled trial protocol.
records.population_setting: Women reporting IPV/fear of partner, urban informal settlement, Nairobi, Kenya (LMIC)
records.key_finding: Community-participatory adaptation found high feasibility and acceptability of a technology-based self-assessment/safety-planning tool in a low-literacy LMIC setting, requiring simplified content, increased visualisation, and delivery via community health volunteers rather than pure self-use.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports transferability of self-check/decision-aid tools to LMIC and non-Western contexts relevant to Thailand, but complicates a pure self-administered (person-alone) Layer 0 model - LMIC adaptation required facilitated/CHV-supported delivery for feasibility.

records.title: Safety decision-making and planning mobile app for intimate partner violence prevention and response: randomised controlled trial in Kenya.
records.design: Randomised, participant-blinded superiority trial, n=352 (177 intervention/175 control), 88.6% retained at 3 months
records.population_setting: Women at risk of/experiencing IPV, Nairobi, Kenya (LMIC, low-resource urban)
records.key_finding: Intervention group had significantly better immediate post-intervention safety preparedness (p=0.001) and 3-month helpfulness of safety strategies (p=0.004); among women with the highest baseline IPV severity, intervention significantly increased resilience (p<0.01) and significantly decreased risk for lethal violence (p<0.01).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports that a facilitated technology-based safety decision tool can improve preparedness and reduce lethal-violence risk in a low-resource setting, directly relevant to the harms/benefit balance for Layer 0 in a non-Western context.

records.title: A tailored online safety and health intervention for women experiencing intimate partner violence: the iCAN Plan 4 Safety randomized controlled trial protocol.
records.population_setting: Canadian women who experienced IPV in previous 6 months, including rural/Indigenous/racialized/immigrant/privacy-prioritising subgroups
records.key_finding: Notes fewer than 1 in 5 Canadian women access safety planning through formal DV services, motivating a tailored, interactive, self-paced online intervention (iCAN) that lets women build risk awareness and a personalised action plan without needing to contact services first.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports the rationale for an anonymous, low-barrier self-check that reaches people who would not otherwise contact a formal service - directly parallel to Layer 0's function as an entry point independent of programme staff.

records.title: Longitudinal impacts of an online safety and health intervention for women experiencing intimate partner violence: randomized controlled trial.
records.population_setting: Adult Canadian women with recent IPV, tailored vs static (non-tailored) version of the same online tool
records.key_finding: Both tailored and static/non-tailored arms improved significantly over time on depression (p<.001) and PTSD (p<.001) and on all secondary outcomes; changes did not differ significantly by study arm despite high self-reported benefit/safety/accessibility ratings in both groups.
records.relevance_to_tphe: complicates the assumption that tailoring/personalised scoring adds outcome benefit over a simpler static self-assessment tool - both versions worked equally well on primary mental-health outcomes, a relevant caution for how elaborate T-PHE's Layer 0 scoring needs to be.

records.title: Design and Development of a Suite of Intimate Partner Violence Screening and Safety Planning Web Apps: User-Centered Approach.
records.population_setting: Marginalized and vulnerable women, design collaboration with intended users, Canada
records.key_finding: Describes user-centred/human-centred design of a suite of 3 app-based IPV screening and safety-planning tools, reporting design challenges and lessons for building mHealth/eHealth tools that let users control access to sensitive content.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports a user-centred, co-design approach for Layer 0's own scored self-check so results and routes are usable and safe for the target population, not just technically anonymous.

records.title: Development and Preliminary Evaluation of iCanPlan: A Mobile Health Application for Intimate Partner Violence Prevention in Thailand.
records.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
records.design: Development + preliminary heuristic expert evaluation (n=30 multidisciplinary experts, 1-month use)
records.population_setting: Thailand; IPV risk-assessment mobile app evaluated by gender-based-violence, social work, psychology, public health and NGO experts
records.key_finding: Experts rated the app highly on usability (mean 4.93/5), safety features (4.73/5) and content quality (4.82/5), with perfect mean scores (5.00/5) for cultural appropriateness, language clarity, ethical considerations and overall evaluation; the app includes an IPV risk-assessment tool, a resource list and educational infographics.
records.relevance_to_tphe: directly supports feasibility and cultural-appropriateness of a scored self-assessment IPV-prevention app in Thailand, the T-PHE setting itself, though evaluation is expert-only (not yet tested with the target population) - a gap the paper itself flags.

records.title: Empowering Safety: The Case for a Decision-making App for Military Partners Facing Intimate Partner Violence.
records.design: Exploratory descriptive survey, single-site convenience sample, n=18
records.population_setting: Female service members and civilian partners, primary care clinic, Fort Bragg, North Carolina, USA
records.key_finding: 9 of 18 participants reported IPV-related experiences in the previous 24 months; awareness/prior use of IPV apps was low, but 13 of 17 respondents expressed interest in a confidential decision-making/safety-support app; authors explicitly caution results are descriptive/hypothesis-generating only, from a small convenience sample.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports demand/acceptability for a confidential decision-support tool even where none currently exists, but at very low evidence level - a caution against overclaiming acceptability data from small convenience samples, relevant to T-PHE's own failure-criterion honesty.
records.evidence_level: descriptive/exploratory survey (low evidence level, explicitly hypothesis-generating)

records.title: Computer-assisted screening for intimate partner violence and control: a randomized trial.
records.design: Randomised trial, blinded outcome assessors, n=293 (144 intervention/149 control)
records.population_setting: Adult women in a current/recent relationship, urban academic family practice clinic, Toronto, Canada
records.key_finding: Baseline prevalence of any IPV/control was 22% (95%CI 17-27%); computer-based self-report screening increased opportunities to discuss IPV (adjusted RR 1.4, CI 1.1-1.9) and increased detection of IPV (adjusted RR 2.0, CI 0.9-4.1) versus standard care.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports that a self-administered computer tool increases disclosure/discussion opportunity relative to unprompted clinical care, an early foundational precedent for anonymous scored self-check mechanisms.

records.title: Electronic Health Record-Based Screening for Intimate Partner Violence: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
records.design: Stepped-wedge cluster RCT, 15 clinics, 8895 unique patients
records.population_setting: Women 18-49y, family medicine primary care clinics, Charleston region, South Carolina, USA
records.key_finding: Noninterruptive EHR alert plus confidential self-administered computer screening increased overall IPV screening rate from 45.2% (10,268/22,730 visits) to 65.3% (22,303/34,157 visits) (RR 1.46, 95%CI 1.44-1.49, p<.001); confidential self-screening detected past-year IPV in 1.5% (130/8895) of patients versus 0.1% (9/17,433) with nurse-led oral screening.
records.relevance_to_tphe: strongly supports that a confidential, self-administered screening channel detects substantially more IPV than a face-to-face/oral route (15-fold higher detection), directly evidencing why Layer 0's anonymous self-held channel should outperform staff-mediated disclosure.

records.title: Risk for Severe Intimate Partner Violence in Nairobi's Informal Settlements: Tailoring the Danger Assessment to Kenya.
records.design: Secondary prospective analysis of myPlan Kenya trial data
records.population_setting: Women in 3 informal settlements, Nairobi, Kenya (LMIC)
records.key_finding: A 16-item Kenya-adapted Danger Assessment (weighted) achieved sensitivity 66.67%, specificity 77.05%, C-statistic 0.78, and all Danger Assessment versions significantly predicted severe IPV at 3-month follow-up (original 20-item: OR 1.26, 95%CI 1.12-1.41).
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports that a scored risk-assessment instrument can be validly tailored and can predict future severe violence in a non-Western LMIC context, relevant methodologically to how T-PHE's own scored self-check items would need local validation rather than direct import.

records.title: Effectiveness of ICT-based intimate partner violence interventions: a systematic review.
records.population_setting: Mixed - internet/mobile/smartphone IPV interventions, including LMIC settings
records.key_finding: ICT-based interventions were found effective mainly for screening, disclosure and prevention; the review explicitly flags a lack of homogeneity in outcome measures, sample sizes and control conditions across studies, and notes unresolved questions on safety, equity and unintended consequences.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports the overall evidence base for technology-delivered IPV screening/self-assessment while explicitly flagging heterogeneity and unresolved safety/equity questions - directly relevant to honestly bounding T-PHE's own claims and failure criterion.

records.title: Web-Based and mHealth Interventions for Intimate Partner Violence Victimization Prevention: A Systematic Review.
records.design: Systematic review, 133 screened, 31 included studies, quality-appraised (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)
records.population_setting: Adults in romantic relationships, mixed web-based and mHealth IPV prevention studies, 1998-2019
records.key_finding: Computer-based screening with or without integrated education was the most common mHealth approach identified across the 31 included studies, spanning primary, secondary and tertiary IPV-victimisation prevention.
records.relevance_to_tphe: supports self-administered computer-based screening as the dominant, established mHealth pattern for IPV prevention internationally, situating Layer 0's self-check within a well-precedented intervention class.

gaps_noted: No PubMed-indexed record found specifically combining 'premarital' status (not-yet-married couples) with a scored anonymous self-check tool - all identified trials enrol women already identifying current/recent partner abuse, not a general premarital population screening before any disclosed problem exists.

Koziol-McLain's iSafe tool and Ford-Gilboe's iCAN Plan 4 Safety component variants did not surface as distinct additional PMIDs beyond the iCAN records already captured; a targeted author-name search (e.g. 'Koziol-McLain' alone) returned 0 results in this session and was not pursued further given time/scope limits - a follow-up search restricted to Koziol-McLain New Zealand SAFvIC/iSafe literature is recommended.

No Thailand-specific RCT or effectiveness (as opposed to preliminary expert-evaluation) data were found for a scored self-check tool; Chuemchit 2026 (PMID 42196762) is development/heuristic-evaluation stage only, not yet tested with the target population or measured for behavioural/health outcomes.

No record was found addressing a combined single self-check instrument spanning fear, control, pressure, reproductive health AND mental health simultaneously (as T-PHE's Layer 0 proposes) - the literature covers these domains via separate, purpose-specific tools (IPV decision aids vs Danger Assessment vs reproductive-coercion measures), not one integrated scored instrument.

Safety-harm data (partner discovery, retaliation) are addressed qualitatively/methodologically (Tarzia 2017) but no record reports a quantified adverse-event rate from an anonymous online self-check specifically, which the T-PHE failure criterion would need.
limits_of_this_search: Search was restricted to PubMed via NCBI E-utilities with English-language, PICO-style queries centred on adult IPV decision-aid and screening literature; grey literature, non-PubMed-indexed Thai-language sources, and non-IPV framed adolescent/premarital relationship-education self-assessment tools (e.g. general SRH knowledge quizzes without an IPV/safety framing) were not systematically searched. Evidence levels above are as stated in each abstract only; no independent methodological quality appraisal was performed beyond what the source study itself reports. This search does not establish that T-PHE's own Layer 0 self-check would be effective - it positions the design choice within existing evidence on structurally similar tools tested in other populations and settings.
